### At[Mercer Forestry Services](https://mercerint.com/our-operations/mercer-forestry-services/) , digital tools support harvesting decisions—but they do not replace field knowledge, preparation or experienced operators.


A harvest plan can identify a stream, a boundary or a steep slope. The more difficult task is translating that information into decisions on the ground.


Before equipment enters a harvest area, crews need to understand the terrain, recognize features that may not be obvious on a map and know what the approved prescription requires them to protect or retain. Once work begins, operators must be able to locate themselves relative to those features and respond to the conditions they encounter.


For[Mercer Forestry Services](https://mercerint.com/our-operations/mercer-forestry-services/) General Manager Marty Hiemstra, a Registered Professional Forester with 30 years of experience, this is where responsible forestry becomes practical.


MFS uses LiDAR data on virtually every harvesting project to develop a more detailed understanding of topography and potential constraints. GPS technology helps crews see where equipment is operating in relation to mapped boundaries, streams and other identified features.


These tools provide valuable information, but they do not capture everything.


> “We do robust ground reconnaissance. There are things that aren’t necessarily recognized on the mapping layers, and that’s where boots on the ground still matter.”


A wet area may be difficult to identify at certain times of the year. Terrain may be more complex than it first appears. A mapped feature may require closer examination before equipment can safely operate nearby.


This combination of digital information and field reconnaissance is especially important on steep or complex terrain. A steep-slope plan may be required, but producing the document is only the beginning. Effective planning requires people to examine the site, identify specific hazards and give crews information they can apply while operating equipment.
